title: Truncated pole normal form
statement: Let $A\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective local map of complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], common uniformizer $\pi\in A$, characteristic zero for $K$, and residue characteristic a prime $p$. Put $k=A/\pi A$ and $l=B/\pi B$, and assume $k=\bigcap_{s\geq0}l^{p^s}$ inside $l$, where $l^{p^s}=\{a^{p^s}:a\in l\}$. Suppose $\zeta\in A$ has order $p$; set $w=1-\zeta$, $P(T)=((1+wT)^p-1)/w^p$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and $e=v_B(w)$ for the normalized integer valuation $v_B(\pi)=1$, extended by $v_B(0)=+\infty$. Let $n,m$ be integers with $0<n<pe$ and $1\leq m\leq\min(n,e,pe-n)$. For $\xi\in L$ with $v_B(\xi)\geq-n$, at least one of the following holds. (i) There exist $c\in L$ and $a\in A$ with $v_B(c)\geq-n/p$ and $\xi+P(c)+w^p\xi P(c)-\pi^{-n}a\in\pi^{-n+m}B$. (ii) There exist an integer $r\geq1$ and a field $K_r=K(t)$ with $t^{p^r}=\pi$, $[K_r:K]=p^r$, such that its integral closure $A_r$ of $A$ is a complete DVR with uniformizer $t$, unchanged residue field, and $\pi A_r=(t)^{p^r}$. This extension is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The tensor product $L_r=L\otimes_KK_r$ is a field, and its integral closure $B_r$ of $B$ is a complete DVR with uniformizer $t$ and residue field $l$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $q=p^r$ and normalize $v_r(t)=1$. There exists $c\in L_r$ with $v_r(c)\geq-nq/p$ such that $\eta=\xi+P(c)+w^p\xi P(c)$ satisfies either $v_r(\eta)\geq-(n-m)q$, or $v_r(\eta)=-d$ for an integer $(n-m)q<d\leq nq$ divisible by $p$ with the residue of $t^d\eta$ not a $p$th power in $l$. Local means pulling back the maximal ideal. No extension generated by a root of $P(T)-\xi$, no minimizing generator, and no ramification-level conclusion is assumed.

The translation in the p-related pair reduction uses the corrected positive sign.

proof.text: Write $v=v_B$ and $H=\pi^{m-n}B$. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus] to $B$: $e>0$, $v(p)=(p-1)e$, and, whenever $v(h)\geq-n/p$ and $v(x)\geq-n$, the transformed parameter $T_h(x):=x+P(h)+w^pxP(h)$ has valuation at least $-n$ and satisfies $T_h(x)\equiv x+h^p-h\pmod H$. Indeed the two discarded terms have valuations at least $e-n$ and $pe-2n$, respectively, both at least $m-n$ by the bounds on $m$. We use the same estimates after base change with $(n,m,e)$ replaced by $(nq,mq,eq)$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, equations first-congruence and second-congruence; Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare

proof.text:
For a finite signed family of elements $h_a$ of valuation at least $-N/p$ in one of these valuation fields, expansion gives
$$\left(\sum_a\epsilon_a h_a\right)^p\equiv\sum_a\epsilon_a h_a^p\pmod{\{x:v(x)\geq M-N\}},\qquad \epsilon_a\in\{1,-1\},$$
where $(N,M,E)$ is $(n,m,e)$ or $(nq,mq,eq)$. Each mixed multinomial coefficient is divisible by the prime $p$, and each product in a degree-$p$ term has valuation at least $-N$. The sign error $\epsilon_a^p-\epsilon_a$ is also divisible by $p$, including $p=2$. Thus every error has valuation at least $(p-1)E-N\geq M-N$, using the valuation of $p$ from [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus] and $M\leq E$. This justifies using Frobenius additivity on these finite sums; it does not assert characteristic $p$ for the fraction field.

source.place: Tag 09F5, the two displayed congruences, expanded binomial-error estimate

proof.text: The field $k=\bigcap_s l^{p^s}$ is perfect: if $a\in k$ and $b^p=a$ in $l$, then for each $s$ choose $u^{p^{s+1}}=a$; injectivity of Frobenius in the field $l$ gives $b=u^{p^s}$, so $b\in k$. Since $v(p)=(p-1)e\geq m$, both $A/\pi^m A$ and $B/\pi^m B$ are nonzero local rings of characteristic $p$ with nilpotent maximal ideals. The induced map is local, since the original map pulls back maximal ideals. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-compatible-truncated-coefficients] to obtain compatible residue sections. Lift the upper section to a set map $\sigma:l\to B$ with $\sigma(0)=0$. It preserves sums and products modulo $\pi^mB$, and $\sigma(k)\subset A+\pi^mB$.

source.place: Tag 09EZ, lemma-cohen; Tag 09F5, compatible sections paragraph

proof.text:
Fix these sections for the rest of the argument. Successively take residues of $\pi^n x$, subtract their lifts, and divide by $\pi$, for $m$ steps. For every $x\in\pi^{-n}B$ this gives
$$x\equiv\sum_{i=n-m+1}^n\sigma(\lambda_i)\pi^{-i}\pmod H.$$
All indices are positive because $m\leq n$. The coefficients are unique: at the largest index with a nonzero coefficient the summand has strictly smaller valuation than all remaining terms, whereas the allowed error has valuation at least $m-n$. Addition of two such expansions adds the coefficients in $l$, since each additive error of $\sigma$ belongs to $\pi^mB$ and $m-i\geq m-n$. Put $J=\{i:\lambda_i\notin k\}$ and $I=\{n-m+1,\ldots,n\}\setminus J$, initially for $x=\xi$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, expansion of xi and definition of I,J

proof.text:
Suppose $j,j'=p^sj$ belong to $J$ with $s>0$. Set
$$h=\sum_{a=0}^{s-1}\sigma(\lambda_j^{p^a})\pi^{-jp^a}.$$
Its largest pole is $j'/p\leq n/p$. Steps 1 and 2, and multiplicativity of $\sigma$ modulo $\pi^m$, give
$$T_h(x)\equiv x-\sigma(\lambda_j)\pi^{-j}+\sigma(\lambda_j^{p^s})\pi^{-j'}\pmod H.$$
In fact each power/lift error has valuation at least $m-jp^{a+1}\geq m-n$, and the internal terms cancel consecutively. Thus only the digits at $j,j'$ change: they become $0$ and $\lambda_{j'}+\lambda_j^{p^s}$. In particular $|J|$ strictly decreases. Repeat until $J$ is empty or no two indices in $J$ differ by a positive power of $p$. This terminates by descent in the nonnegative integer $|J|$; the sections, $n,m,H$ stay fixed and every parameter remains in $\pi^{-n}B$. The positive sign of $h$ is essential.

proof.text: All these translations are a single allowed translation. Start with $c_0=0$ and replace $c_0$ by $c_0\star h=c_0+h+wc_0h$ at each step. If both inputs have valuation at least $-n/p$, their product term has valuation at least $e-2n/p>-n/p$; hence the bound persists. The identity in [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus] gives exactly $T_h(T_{c_0}(\xi))=T_{c_0\star h}(\xi)$ by expansion. Denote the resulting parameter by $x=T_{c_0}(\xi)$ and its final digits by $\lambda_i$. If $J=\varnothing$, choose $a_i\in A$ lifting the lower section values, so $\sigma(\lambda_i)-a_i\in\pi^mB$. Then $a=\sum_i a_i\pi^{n-i}\in A$ satisfies $x-\pi^{-n}a\in H$. Taking $c=c_0$ proves alternative (i), including its valuation bound.

proof.text: Construct $D=A[T]/(T^q-\pi)$, $t=[T]$. Its defining polynomial is Eisenstein: its lower coefficients lie in $\pi A$ and its constant coefficient $-\pi$ does not lie in $\pi^2A$. By [lem-sfb-eisenstein-quotient-dvr], $D$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $(t)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] it has the $A$-basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{q-1}$. Localizing this basis gives the domain $K[T]/(T^q-\pi)$ of dimension $q$, which is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. It is $K(t)=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, so $[K(t):K]=q$, and $T^q-\pi$ is the minimal polynomial of $t$. Its constant term is nonzero, and $q\geq2$.

source.place: Tag 09EV, lemma-pull-root-uniformizer, proof of (1)-(5); Tag 09F5, chosen root extension

proof.text:
Over the characteristic-zero field $K$, $f=T^q-\pi$ satisfies the Bezout identity
$$-\pi^{-1}f+(q\pi)^{-1}T f'=1.$$
Thus $f$ is separable by [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Since $K(t)=K[t]$, [lem-trf-simple-separable-field-extension] proves that $K_r:=K(t)$ is a separable algebraic extension of $K$. In $D$, $t^q=\pi$ and $D/(t)=A/(\pi)$; consequently $A\to D$ is local, its residue field is $k$, and $(\pi)D=(t)^q$. Apply the uniqueness clause of [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization] with $V=D$ and the finite extension $K_r/K$: $A_r=D$ is the integral closure, and it is complete for its own maximal ideal. This proves all the requested assertions about $A_r$ and $K_r$.

source.place: Tag 09EV, lemma-pull-root-uniformizer; Tag 09EM, remark-construction (completeness); Fields Tag 09H9

proof.text: Now apply [lem-sfb-epp-totally-ramified-base-change] to $A\to B$ and $K_r/K$. Its hypotheses hold: both DVRs are complete, $\pi$ generates both maximal ideals, the field extension is finite separable, and the just-constructed $A_r$ has residue field $k$ and $(\pi)A_r=(t)^q$. It gives that $L_r=L\otimes_K K_r$ is a field, and that $B_r=B\otimes_A A_r$ is its integral closure of $B$, is a complete DVR with uniformizer $t$, and has residue field $l$. The normalized valuation $v_r$ restricts to $qv$ on $L$: a $B$-unit remains a unit in $B_r$ and $\pi=t^q$. In particular $v_r(w)=eq$.

For $i\in I$, perfectness of $k$ gives $
u_i\in k$ with $
u_i^q=\lambda_i$; put $x_i=\sigma(
u_i)$. For $j\in J$, put $y_j=\sigma(\mu_j)$. Multiplicativity of the section modulo $\pi^mB$ gives $\sigma(\lambda_i)\equiv x_i^q$ and $\sigma(\lambda_j)\equiv y_j^{p^{r_j}}$ modulo $\pi^mB$. Multiplying by a pole $\pi^{-i}$ with $i\leq n$ gives errors in $\pi^{m-n}B_r=t^{(m-n)q}B_r=:H_r$. Since $t^q=\pi$ exactly, the final expansion of $x$ becomes
$$x\equiv\sum_{i\in I}(x_it^{-i})^{p^r}+\sum_{j\in J}(y_jt^{-d_j})^{p^{r_j}}\pmod {H_r}.$$
The same section and its chosen lifts are used throughout.

source.place: Tag 09F5, two expansions after adjoining pi prime

proof.text:
For an element $u$ and integer $s\geq0$, write $S(u,s)=\sum_{a=0}^{s-1}u^{p^a}$, with $S(u,0)=0$. Set
$$h=-\sum_{i\in I}S(x_it^{-i},r)-\sum_{j\in J}S(y_jt^{-d_j},r_j).$$
Every summand has pole at most $nq/p$: in the first sum its largest possible pole is $iq/p\leq nq/p$; in the second nonempty sum it is $d_jp^{r_j-1}=jq/p\leq nq/p$. Hence $v_r(h)\geq-nq/p$. Apply the signed expansion in step 2 with $N=nq,M=mq,E=eq$. Consecutive powers cancel, so
$$h^p-h\equiv-\sum_{i\in I}(x_it^{-i})^q+\sum_{i\in I}x_it^{-i}-\sum_{j\in J}(y_jt^{-d_j})^{p^{r_j}}+\sum_{j\in J}y_jt^{-d_j}\pmod{H_r}.$$
For $r_j=0$ the corresponding difference on the right is zero. Step 1 and step 11 therefore give
$$\eta:=T_h(x)\equiv\sum_{i\in I}x_it^{-i}+\sum_{j\in J}y_jt^{-d_j}\pmod{H_r}.$$
In particular $v_r(\eta)\geq-nq$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, final z_1 and xi prime calculation, including mixed-characteristic binomial errors

proof.text: Let $d=\max_{j\in J}d_j$. If $d\leq(n-m)q$, all displayed poles are at most $(n-m)q$, since $i\leq n<d$ for $i\in I$; thus $v_r(\eta)\geq-(n-m)q$. Otherwise the unique summand of pole $d$ is $y_{j_0}t^{-d}$, where $d_{j_0}=d$. All other summands, and the error in $H_r$, have strictly larger valuation. Since the residue of $y_{j_0}$ is $\mu_{j_0}\notin l^p$, it is nonzero; hence $v_r(\eta)=-d$ and $\overline{t^d\eta}=\mu_{j_0}\notin l^p$. Step 7 gives $p\mid d$ and $d\leq nq$. Finally take $c=c_0+h+wc_0h$ in $L_r$. Its valuation is at least $-nq/p$, because $v_r(c_0)\geq-nq/p$ and $eq-2nq/p>-nq/p$. The exact composition identity from step 6 yields $T_c(\xi)=T_h(T_{c_0}(\xi))=\eta$. This proves (ii) for the original $\xi$.
